messages:
From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@summitfin.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SIG/CAIQ follow-up: KMS sampling & transport proof request

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the earlier SIG response — the questionnaire review went well. The audit team has asked for a small sampling of artifacts related to key lifecycle and transport for our CAIQ supplement. Specifically they're requesting: 

- An export (sample) of the last 90 days of KMS provisioning/deprovisioning events tied to tenant IDs (redacted where necessary)
- Proof of TLS configuration for data-in-transit endpoints (cipher list + TLS version snapshot)
- The latest HSM attestation statement and the documented rotation runbook we can reference in our SOC2 evidence collection

Can you confirm whether you can provide a small redacted export and an HSM attestation by next Friday? If you need a formal NDA or additional context, let me know.

Appreciate it — this is for the June 2028 SOC2 refresh bucket.

— Maria
Lead Vendor Risk Analyst
Summit Financial
(attachment: audit_request_summary.pdf)

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@summitfin.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com, jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 08:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ follow-up: KMS sampling & transport proof request

Hi Maria —

We can provide the artifacts you listed. Quick notes on scope and redaction: 

- KMS events: we will export provisioning/deprovisioning and rotation events for the last 90 days. Tenant identifiers will be pseudonymized (tenant_xxx) except for the account you indicated. We will include event timestamps, actor (service-account or user), and operation type. CSV sample will be attached.
- TLS snapshot: we will include the cipher list and TLS versions in use for our public endpoints and the internal ingress used for model traffic (transport snapshot JSON).
- HSM attestation: we will attach the vendor attestation statement and the rotation runbook PDF.

I am looping in Jasmine (Security) to confirm the redaction approach and Karthik (Infra) for the export. We aim to have the initial package to you by EOD Friday (2027-12-04). If Summit needs a signed attestation, please share the template.

Next steps:
1) Jasmine — can you confirm redaction fields and whether we need additional access logs for the tenant sample?
2) Karthik — can you generate the 90-day KMS event export and a short digest of the rotation windows?

Thanks,

Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
(attachment: request_acknowledgement.txt)

From: jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com, laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ follow-up: KMS sampling & transport proof request

Vanessa / Laura —

Redaction approach: we will replace tenant account IDs with deterministic pseudonyms (tenant_001, tenant_002) and remove any PII. We should keep internal service-account IDs and role names to demonstrate separation of duties, but obfuscate API keys and any full GUIDs that could be traced externally.

Checklist for artifacts: 
- KMS sampling CSV: columns = event_ts, tenant_pseudonym, operation, actor_type, actor_id_pseudonym, key_id_hash, rotation_epoch, notes.
- Rotation runbook: shows scheduled rotation window (monthly automated rotations for ephemeral tenant keys; quarterly for platform master keys), emergency rotation steps, and rollback guidance.
- HSM attestation: vendor-signed PEM statement included; any sensitive serials redacted.
- TLS snapshot: include accepted ciphers and minimum TLS versions per endpoint; sign-off that mutual-TLS is enabled for Dedicated deployments.

I'll review the CSV sample once Karthik has it. Aim to return a redaction-reviewed package before Friday midday.

— Jasmine Liu
Security Controls Lead, Redwood Inference
(attachment: redaction_guidance.md)

From: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
To: jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 3 Dec 2027 15:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ follow-up: KMS sampling & transport proof request

Team —

Export prepared and attached (sample of 90 days). Key points for the package: 
- Export includes provisioning, deprovisioning, create_key, rotate_key events for 2027-09-05 -> 2027-11-30.
- We replaced tenant IDs with tenant_001..tenant_012 (Deterministic mapping in provenance_map.txt — not shared externally).
- key_id stored as a SHA256 hash to avoid exposing raw key material (hashes are one-way).
- Rotation schedule notes: platform master keys: quarterly rolling with HSM-enforced wrap; tenant ephemeral keys: monthly auto-rotation and expire after 45 days if unused.
- Transit snapshot captures TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 enabled; preferred cipher suites listed. Mutual-TLS enforced on Dedicated routes.

Attachments in this internal draft: kms_sampling_export_20271204.csv (sample 250 rows), transit_tls_snapshot_20271130.json, rotation_runbook_v2.1.pdf, hsm_attestation_statement_2027-11-15.txt.

Vanessa — handing to you and Jasmine to run the redaction checks and sign-off for handover.

Karthik
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: kms_sampling_export_20271204.csv)

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com

Maria —

Thanks for your patience. Attached is the redaction-reviewed evidence package for Summit Financial's CAIQ/SIG follow-up. Highlights: 

- kms_sampling_export_20271204.csv (purpose-built sample with pseudonymized tenant IDs; includes event_ts, operation, actor_type, key_id_hash, rotation_epoch) (attachment)
- rotation_runbook_v2.1.pdf (describes automated monthly tenant key rotation and quarterly master key rotation; emergency rotation playbook included) (attachment)
- hsm_attestation_statement_2027-11-15.txt (vendor-signed attestation; serials redacted) (attachment)
- transit_tls_snapshot_20271130.json (cipher suites and TLS versions; note that TLS 1.3 is preferred and TLS 1.2 is allowed for legacy edge proxies) (attachment)

A couple of clarifications we documented in an internal provenance note: we pseudonymize tenant IDs for external deliveries by policy; if Summit requires explicit tenant mapping we can provide a controlled mapping under a signed NDA and scoped access request.

If the audit team needs an executed attestation (wet signature) or a short cover letter on Redwood letterhead, let me know and Laura can coordinate.

Best,

Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
